get.description: The named readyForPublication worklist and count require caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager, including saved-query links. Other authenticated roles receive 403 before reads or side effects. Ordinary filters and field conditions are unchanged.

parameters.description: Which tab of the case list to return: `all` (All applications), `open` (Open), `received` (Received), `enroled` (Enroled), `returned` (Returned), `awaitingConfirmation` (Awaiting confirmation), `readyForPublication` (Ready for publication). An unrecognised or repeated value falls back to `all` rather than being refused, because the key comes from a URL a caseworker may have bookmarked -- the response echoes the key that was actually applied, so the fallback is observable. ANDs with `q` and every `where` condition. `awaitingConfirmation` is the cases still waiting for an applicant's reply to the Request confirmation to proceed email, and each row on it carries `daysAwaitingConfirmation`. `readyForPublication` selects `publishToLondonGazette=true`, `dateNoticeSentToLondonGazette` absent and `state=Enroled`, excluding `type=DeedOfRelinquishment`; other types, including unset types, are unchanged. This named worklist and its count require caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager (403 otherwise), including saved-query links. Its default sort is `dateEnroled:asc` (oldest enrolled first), unless the caller supplies `sort`.
parameters.name: filter

parameters.description: A condition, as `field:operator:value`. Repeat the parameter for more than one; they are ANDed, and there is no OR. Split on the first two colons only, so a colon inside a value survives. The field must be a queryable case field and the operator must apply to its kind, or the request is a 400 naming every condition it could not read rather than only the first. Operators: is (takes one value), contains (takes one value), startsWith (takes one value), before (takes one value), after (takes one value), gt (takes one value), lt (takes one value), between (takes two comma-separated values, low first), isOneOf (takes at least one comma-separated value), isEmpty (takes no value), isNotEmpty (takes no value).
parameters.name: where

parameters.description: A search term. Matched against the case reference exactly -- tolerant of case, hyphens and spaces, so `kbdp2026-10100` and `KBDP202610100` find the same case -- or as a case-insensitive substring of newForename, newSurname, oldForename, oldSurname, parents, representativeName. Those two are ORed, and the result is ANDed with `filter` and every `where` condition. Matching is substring and not fuzzy: a misspelling does not match. Addresses and narrative fields are deliberately not searched. Longer than 100 characters is truncated rather than refused. Where the term matched one case's reference exactly, the response's `referenceMatch` carries that case's id.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: An order, as `field:asc|desc`. The direction may be omitted and defaults to ascending. Sortable fields are the columns the list shows: referencenumber, displayReference, dateOfApplication, inPerson, postCounter, feeReference, dateReceived, type, maritalStatus, minorDateOfBirth, ageOfMinor, ageOfMinorMonths, parents, privacy, state, currentReferralState, urgency, urgencyreason, onlineApplicationReference, retainPermanently, awaitingFurtherDocsInfo, newForename, newMiddleName, newSurname, oldForename, oldMiddleName, oldSurname, applicantBuildingNoName, applicantAddress1, applicantAddress2, applicantTownCity, applicantPostcode, applicantEmail, applicantTelephone, representativeName, representativeCompany, representativeEmail, representativeTelephone, representativeBuildingNoName, representativeAddress1, representativeAddress2, representativeTownCity, representativePostcode, nationality, nationalitySection, nationalitySectionOther, dateOfDeclaration, referToMasterChoice, dateReadyForMaster, dateReferred, referralNotes, masterName, masterDirections, masterDecision, masterDateOfDecision, dateDecisionDirectionsReceived, publishToLondonGazette, signatureRequestedDate, signatureReceivedDate, dateEnroled, dateNoticeSentToLondonGazette, dateReturned, returnReason, refundAmount, dateOfRefund, refundReference, awaitingConfirmationSince, createdOn, modifiedOn, createdBy, modifiedBy. Defaults to newest first, except on the `awaitingConfirmation` filter, which defaults to `awaitingConfirmationSince:asc` -- longest wait first.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: The page to return, 1-based. Defaults to 1.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many rows on the page. Defaults to 25 and is capped at 100: a larger value is clamped to the cap rather than refused, because an unbounded list is a denial of service against the service's own database.
parameters.name: size

direction.description: Whether the document was received or sent. Optional.

documentTypeId.description: The document type this file is filed under. Must be an existing type, or 404. A type's applicability to the case's marital status and deed poll type is advisory -- it is what a form filters its options by, and the service does not enforce it.

file.description: The file. A PDF, image or Word document, within the configured size limit.

name.description: An optional display name. Defaults to the uploaded filename, capped to the column.

requestBody.description: The file and the document row to record against it.

409.description: This case is not ready for documents yet, because it has no CCD case. Try again once it has been linked.

parameters.description: Which email. Matched exactly -- a near miss is a 404 naming what would have been accepted, because this token is a value the caller read out of GET /caseworker/cases/{id}/emails. One of: application-rejected (Application rejected), request-confirmation-to-proceed (Request confirmation to proceed), chase-missing-documents (Chase missing documents), forms-for-completion-adult (Forms for completion), forms-for-completion-minor (Forms for completion for a child). That GET is also where a client learns which of them this case may have sent and whether this environment can send it at all: a template it reports as inapplicable is a 409 here, and an unprovisioned one fails at GOV.UK Notify.
parameters.name: template

parameters.description: Which compose journey this send belongs to. One journey creates one UUID and sends it with every retry of this POST -- a timed-out request, a double-click, a resubmit after a validation failure -- and a later journey creates another: that is what lets one case be chased twice on purpose while a double-click still sends one email. A repeat of the same key for the same case and the same content answers 200 with the first receipt and enqueued=false; the same key with different content is a 409, because the header and the body then contradict each other; a missing or unparseable key is a 400 naming this header. Do not generate a fresh UUID per request -- that satisfies this schema and loses the protection entirely.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: The email is not applicable, the request key conflicts, or a contradictory email is already owed. For CDAM forms, the case may be unlinked, its deed preparation unavailable or uncertain, or material case inputs changed during preparation. Retained deeds are never regenerated by retrying.

502.description: The forms template is unconfigured or the deed upload/attachment could not be confirmed. Its preparation is retained; review its storage outcome before retrying. No email is enqueued by an unconfirmed preparation.

post.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Checks recipient, readiness, reservations and configuration. Returns a 30-minute comparison token. No reservations, uploads or notes are written.

get.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Newest submission first, then descending batch ID. Legacy sent batches remain in sent history. Page defaults to 1; size defaults to 25, capped at 100.

Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Batches are newest first, with frozen case references and display-name attribution. At most 100 references per batch, in lexical display order, with referencesTruncated indicating omitted members. This is not send order. No custom filtering or sorting.

parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1; defaults to 1.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Rows per page; defaults to 25 and is capped at 100.
parameters.name: size

post.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Sending is disabled by default. When configured and enabled, a fresh confirmed request makes at most one email attempt. Repeats resolve recorded status only. 202 means Preparing/Sending; 200 means terminal, not necessarily sent. Reuse the original key and body after a lost response. Never retry an uncertain request with a new key.
post.summary: Submit or resolve a Gazette request

get.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Includes legacy sent batches, with unknown submission, recipient and group facts null. Sent means accepted by Notify, not delivered or published.
Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Reference then case ID ordering, independent of live cases. Page defaults to 1; size defaults to 25, capped at 100. Includes legacy batches.
get.summary: Read all frozen Gazette batch references

get.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Initially recipient and attribution are null, revision 0.

put.description: Requires caseworker-deedpoll-delivery-manager. Supply the revision read with the form; stale revisions return 409 without changes. Each changed address increments revision and records attribution. Saving the current address at the current revision is a no-op. No email is sent.

CreateCaseRequest.description: Every field is optional: a case is logged incrementally. An omitted field is left alone and an explicit null clears the column, where the column is nullable. Unknown keys are ignored. dateReceived is needed to allocate a reference number, so a create without it is a 400 attributed to that field.

CreateNoteRequest.description: The note text. Trimmed before validation, and the trimmed value is what is stored. The author comes from the caller's token and the case from the path, so neither can be set here. Unknown keys are ignored.

CreateReferralRequest.description: A referral of the case to the judiciary, raised unclaimed into the shared pool. reasons is the only field required outright; notes is required when Other is among them, and urgencyReason when urgency is Urgent. The case comes from the path, the state is always Open, and there is no target judge -- who picks a referral up is a later transition -- so state, migrated and any assignee are ignored rather than refused, as any unknown key is. A case may hold many referrals over its lifetime but only one that is not closed or withdrawn, so a second live referral is a 409 rather than a 400.

notes.description: The single free-text field: the explanation Other requires and the general referral note at once, rather than two near-identical fields. Trimmed, and a whitespace-only value counts as none.

reasons.description: Why the case is being referred. At least one, de-duplicated, and stored in the order they are sent. Other requires notes.

items.description: Matched exactly, as the stored form is the wire form.

urgency.description: The referral's own urgency, separate from the case's and defaulting to Normal. Matched exactly: an unknown value is refused rather than read as Normal, because that would drop the one signal that gets a referral looked at.

urgencyReason.description: Why the referral jumped the queue. Required when urgency is Urgent.

CreateSavedQueryRequest.description: A saved case-list query. Only name is required: a query that narrows nothing is legitimate, because "everything, newest first" is a view somebody wants a tab for. The owner comes from the caller's token, so ownerId cannot be set here, and page is not part of a view -- both are ignored rather than refused, as any unknown key is. Saving does not select: the new query is in the library and in nobody's list, including its owner's.

conditions.description: The where conditions as the wire strings a list URL carried -- "field:operator:value", split on the first two colons -- and NOT structured objects. Validated on write by the same parser a live query goes through, so a saved query round-trips a list URL unchanged.

filter.description: Which case-list filter tab the view opens on.

name.description: What the query is called, as it appears in a navigation bar.

searchTerm.description: The q search term this view carries, matched against the reference and the name columns. page is deliberately not stored: page 4 of a previous result set is not a page of this one.

shared.description: Whether the query is published to the library every caseworker can browse. Publishing makes it findable, not present in anyone else's list -- each user selects what they want to see. A shared query may also be amended or deleted by an Administrator.

sortDirection.description: Matched exactly: asc, desc. A bare sortField with no direction is read as ascending.

sortField.description: The field to order by. Any of CaseSort.sortableFields() -- the single-valued form fields plus the audit columns -- which is not enumerated here because there are more than sixty and a frozen copy would drift.

CreateWitnessRequest.description: A witness or declarant. All four fields are required: every column is NOT NULL. declarant must be a JSON boolean -- the string "true" is refused rather than coerced. Values are stored as submitted and not trimmed. The case comes from the path and no author is recorded, so neither can be set here. Unknown keys are ignored.

declarant.description: Whether this witness is the declarant. One row type covers both.

witnessAddress.description: The whole address as one free-text field, exactly as the source form holds it.

body.description: The wording GOV.UK Notify rendered as plain text. The applicant received branded HTML.

notifyState.description: Outbox state. Sent means accepted by GOV.UK Notify; it does not mean delivered.

JudicialDirectionRequest.description: The holding judge's direction on a referral, recorded once and complete -- there is no draft and no patch, because the check-your-answers page and the attestation are the admin's. Permitted only on a referral this caller currently holds, so a referral withdrawn under them or taken back by the inactivity sweep is a 409 rather than a late direction on a referral that moved on. The referral comes from the path and the case is resolved from it -- a judicial URL carries no case id -- and the state, decidedBy and decisionDate come from the transition, the token and the clock, so all of them are ignored rather than refused, as any unknown key is.

decision.description: What the judge decided. Matched exactly, as the stored form is the wire form.

directionsText.description: What the judge directed. Optional: an approval that needs no comment is a real answer. Trimmed, and a whitespace-only value counts as none.

publishToGazette.description: Whether the change is to be published in the London Gazette. The judge's decision, never derived from a caseworker's referral reasons. A JSON boolean -- the string "false" is refused rather than coerced, because publication cannot be taken back.

PreviewEmailRequest.description: The slots a caseworker fills in, and the whole of what a client may set. Every other value in the email -- the reference number, the applicant's former names, and which refund paragraph is rendered -- is resolved from the case, and a request naming one of them is a 400 that says which: a caseworker altering the reference an applicant is told, or flipping the refund branch, is a correctness and a fraud problem rather than a convenience. An unknown key is likewise refused and named rather than ignored, unlike every other body here. judges_reason is required of the email but not of the request: it is pre-populated from the referral's direction, so a body omitting it is accepted whenever a direction was recorded, and refused with that field named when none was. documents_required is required of the request itself -- nothing pre-populates it -- so an empty body for that email is a 400. The properties here are every slot any template takes, which is not the set any one template takes: which slots a given template accepts, and what they open with, come from GET /caseworker/cases/{id}/emails, and a slot belonging to another template is refused by name. An over-long slot is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated quotation of a judge is worse than being asked to shorten one.

additional_notes.description: Optional. Anything the caseworker wants to add to the approved wording.

documents_required.description: Required of the request, and pre-populated from nothing -- this email exists to tell the applicant what is still needed, and only a caseworker can say what that is. An omitted or blank value is a 400 naming this field.

judges_reason.description: Required of the email but not of the request: pre-populated from the referral's direction, so a body omitting it is accepted whenever a direction was recorded and refused with this field named when none was.

RecordConfirmationRequest.description: The applicant's answer to the Request confirmation to proceed email, as the caseworker who read their reply records it. Recording it does not move the case on: no date is set or cleared, and the caseworker then does whatever the process requires through the ordinary case edit. Idempotent by refusal rather than last-write-wins -- a second answer is a 409 naming what is already recorded and when, and an answer on a referral that was never asked to confirm is a 409 too. The referral comes from the path, and the recording caseworker and the date come from the token and the clock, so confirmationRecordedBy and confirmationReceivedAt are ignored rather than refused, as any unknown key is.

note.description: What the caseworker wants the case timeline to say about the reply. Optional -- the outcome is the fact -- trimmed, and a whitespace-only value counts as none.

outcome.description: What the applicant answered. Matched exactly, as the stored form is the wire form: Confirmed means they still want the deed enrolled knowing it will be published, and Withdrawn that they do not and want a refund.

SendEmailRequest.description: The slots a caseworker fills in, and the whole of what a client may set. Every other value in the email -- the reference number, the applicant's former names, and which refund paragraph is rendered -- is resolved from the case, and a request naming one of them is a 400 that says which: a caseworker altering the reference an applicant is told, or flipping the refund branch, is a correctness and a fraud problem rather than a convenience. An unknown key is likewise refused and named rather than ignored, unlike every other body here. judges_reason is required of the email but not of the request: it is pre-populated from the referral's direction, so a body omitting it is accepted whenever a direction was recorded, and refused with that field named when none was. documents_required is required of the request itself -- nothing pre-populates it -- so an empty body for that email is a 400. The properties here are every slot any template takes, which is not the set any one template takes: which slots a given template accepts, and what they open with, come from GET /caseworker/cases/{id}/emails, and a slot belonging to another template is refused by name. An over-long slot is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated quotation of a judge is worse than being asked to shorten one.

additional_notes.description: Optional. Anything the caseworker wants to add to the approved wording.

documents_required.description: Required of the request, and pre-populated from nothing -- this email exists to tell the applicant what is still needed, and only a caseworker can say what that is. An omitted or blank value is a 400 naming this field.

judges_reason.description: Required of the email but not of the request: pre-populated from the referral's direction, so a body omitting it is accepted whenever a direction was recorded and refused with this field named when none was.

selectionFingerprint.description: Exact opaque token returned by preview; retain it with the same key on a retry.

UpdateCaseRequest.description: A patch: an omitted field is left alone, an explicit null clears the column where the column is nullable, and unknown keys are ignored. referencenumber, displayReference and the audit columns are not writable. privacy is honoured only for a caller entitled to set it, and state is re-derived from the merged dates.

recipientEmail.description: One email address; outer whitespace is trimmed. Local part is at most 64 characters. Null and blank are refused.

revision.description: The revision returned by the settings read; stale values return 409.

UpdateNoteRequest.description: An empty patch is accepted and re-stamps modifiedBy. An explicit null for note is a 400, not a clear: the column is NOT NULL. Unknown keys are ignored.

UpdateSavedQueryRequest.description: A patch. An omitted field is left as stored, and an explicit null clears the column -- unlike the note and witness patches, where no column is nullable and a null is a 400. name cannot be cleared. An empty patch is accepted and re-stamps modifiedOn. Editing is the owner's right, or an Administrator's if the query is shared. Unknown keys are ignored.

conditions.description: The where conditions as the wire strings a list URL carried -- "field:operator:value", split on the first two colons -- and NOT structured objects. Validated on write by the same parser a live query goes through, so a saved query round-trips a list URL unchanged.

filter.description: Which case-list filter tab the view opens on.

name.description: What the query is called, as it appears in a navigation bar.

searchTerm.description: The q search term this view carries, matched against the reference and the name columns. page is deliberately not stored: page 4 of a previous result set is not a page of this one.

shared.description: Whether the query is published to the library every caseworker can browse. Publishing makes it findable, not present in anyone else's list -- each user selects what they want to see. A shared query may also be amended or deleted by an Administrator.

sortDirection.description: Matched exactly: asc, desc. A bare sortField with no direction is read as ascending.

sortField.description: The field to order by. Any of CaseSort.sortableFields() -- the single-valued form fields plus the audit columns -- which is not enumerated here because there are more than sixty and a frozen copy would drift.

UpdateWitnessRequest.description: A patch. An omitted field is left as stored; a field that is present gets the create rule. An empty patch is accepted and re-stamps modifiedOn. An explicit null is a 400, not a clear: every column is NOT NULL. Unknown keys are ignored.

declarant.description: Whether this witness is the declarant. One row type covers both.

witnessAddress.description: The whole address as one free-text field, exactly as the source form holds it.
